When one penetrates both nature and characteristics as being like a shadow—realizing they are universally identical and non-dual—one enters the gate of the illusory birth of wisdom. This is the vision of Lady Māyā.
It is like when the youth Sudhana asked Lady Māyā, "How long has it been since you attained this liberation? to which Māyā replied, "Good son..."
My son, it was in ages long past, beyond the reach of inconceivable time and unknown even to the supernatural powers and divine eye of Bodhisattvas in their final birth—knowable only by a Buddha.
This is intended to clarify that it cannot be known through temporal divisions, nor can it be measured by the number of kalpas.
It must be realized through the seal of Buddha-wisdom, wherein the distinctions between ancient and modern are exhausted and the boundaries of beginning and end vanish.
One is able to know the duration—whether long or short—of the attainment of the Dharma upon generating the resolve.
If one were to establish a view of its beginning and end, even if one were to compare it to the number of atoms in inexhaustible lands, there would be no way to fully comprehend it.

Even if one were to further compare it to the number of atoms in an infinite succession of inexhaustible lands, it still could not be fully comprehended. Only when numbers vanish and calculations reach their limit does wisdom manifest, and only then is it known; that is, it is non-existent.

One calculates their distance by means of numerical methods. Even if one were to employ mathematical calculations for an exhaustive or inexhaustible number of kalpas to calculate the measure of empty space within a single pore, one would find no limit to it, because empty space has no measure of duration.
It is by this immeasurability that time is attained. There was an evil Māra named Suvarṇaprabha, who was accompanied by his retinue of immeasurable hosts.

He arrived at the place where the Bodhisattva was. That Greatly Majestic Universal Monarch (Cakravartin), having already attained the sovereign power of a bodhisattva’s supernatural faculties (*abhijñā*), manifested a host of soldiers many times greater in number, who surrounded the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*). All the Māras were struck with terror and fled in all directions.

This clarifies that the evil Māra named Golden Light (*Suvarṇaprabha*) is, in reality, the realm of the wisdom of the Dharma-body (*dharmakāya*); in truth and falsehood, they are of one single mark, eternally free from defilement.
The Bodhisattva has not yet clarified the equality of mind and its objects; they must rely upon the King of All-Knowledge to clearly contemplate mind and objects.
When the principle is thoroughly realized as non-dual, mind and objects are like illusions. All objective realms are produced by illusory wisdom; thus, one is not deluded regarding objects.

The demons of conceptual thought and the mind are entirely the Dharma-realm, all of which constitute Buddha-activity. This is called "dispersing the scattered. [Thus it is] for the youth Sudhana. Combined.
From the section beginning with "Palms Joined in Reverence" down to the end of the fascicle, it clarifies that Sudhana has already resolved upon the Great Bodhicitta.
It explains the meaning of the "Inconceivable Section on the Power and Merit of the Roots of Goodness of Bodhicitta," as praised by Maitreya;

it demonstrates that all supernatural powers, spiritual faculties, and the myriad practices of a bodhisattva have Bodhicitta as their foundation for extinguishing birth and death and cutting off the flow of suffering.
The eighty-four thousand gates of affliction are purified, and the ocean of all-knowledge is manifested and perfected;
all of these take the bodhicitta as their root. Because the bodhicitta is without dependence and without abiding, no essence, arising, or ceasing can be found.
Since the bodhicitta is without dependence, wisdom is also without dependence. Since wisdom is without dependence, all that is performed is without a performer.

Abiding therein, one attains realization; by this, the karma of birth and death perishes, and there is only the sovereignty of wisdom. The myriad practices of great compassion arise from wisdom. The essence of wisdom has no dependence;

the myriad practices are like transformations, and the benefiting of sentient beings is like an illusion. The power of the divine paths and spiritual faculties is like the moon in the sky appearing universally in all waters:
the essence of wisdom does not go forth, nor do the "water" of the sentient beings' minds come toward it; they appear according to the purity of their own karma.
It is of the same essence as wisdom. According to the depth or shallowness of one's purity, the manifestations of wisdom differ; it is neither this nor that.

If you wish to behold the ocean of wisdom of the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas of the ten directions, simply purify the karmic conditions of the twelve links of existence, and the Buddha-wisdom will manifest of itself.
When one seeks only other superior realms, one's own Dharma becomes obscured.

That Maitreya Bodhisattva snapped his fingers and the gate opened immediately signifies that when the dust of delusion is lost and attachments depart, the Dharma-gate opens of its own accord. That once Sudhana had entered, the gate closed again signifies...
Because wisdom has no interior, exterior, or middle; no exiting or entering; and no delusion or realization, it is called "returning-closure.
As the Sūtra says: "The bodhicitta is the birthplace of the Bodhisattva; Prajñā is the birth-mother; Upāya is the father;
the perfection of Dāna is the wet-nurse; the observance of Śīla is the foster-mother; Kṣānti is the adornment; Vīrya is the nurturer; and Dhyāna..."
Concentration is his bath; virtuous friends are his preceptors; bodhicitta is his companion; all wholesome deeds are his retinue;
and bodhisattvas are his brothers. Such as these are the birthplaces of a bodhisattva.

That this person’s long-standing obstacles have been eliminated and they shall immediately be reborn in the Pure Land, as attested by the Three Jewels.
